sentences.zh: 世祖九王 高宗二十九王 後主十一子

translations.literal: Nine Princes of Emperor Wen; Twenty-nine Princes of Emperor Xuan; Eleven Sons of Houzhu
translations.idiomatic: Nine Princes of Emperor Wen; Twenty-nine Princes of Emperor Xuan; Eleven Sons of Houzhu

sentences.zh: 世祖十三男：沈皇后生廢帝、始興王伯茂，嚴淑媛生鄱陽王伯山、晉安王伯恭，潘容華生新安王伯固，劉昭華生衡陽王伯信，王充華生廬陵王伯仁，張脩容生江夏王伯義，韓脩華生武陵王伯禮，江貴妃生永陽王伯智，孔貴妃生桂陽王伯謀。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen had thirteen sons: the Deposed Emperor and the Prince of Shixing Bo Mao were born to Empress Shen; the Prince of Poyang Bo Shan and the Prince of Jin'an Bo Gong to Lady Yan the Honored Consort; the Prince of Xin'an Bo Gu to Lady Pan the Graceful Beauty; the Prince of Hengyang Bo Xin to Lady Liu the Bright Beauty; the Prince of Luling Bo Ren to Lady Wang the Filling Beauty; the Prince of Jiangxia Bo Yi to Lady Zhang the Cultivated Beauty; the Prince of Wuling Bo Li to Lady Han the Cultivated Beauty; the Prince of Yongyang Bo Zhi to Lady Jiang the Honored Consort; the Prince of Guiyang Bo Mou to Lady Kong the Honored Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had thirteen sons. Empress Shen bore the Deposed Emperor and Bo Mao, Prince of Shixing. Lady Yan the Honored Consort bore Bo Shan, Prince of Poyang, and Bo Gong, Prince of Jin'an. Lady Pan the Graceful Beauty bore Bo Gu, Prince of Xin'an. Lady Liu the Bright Beauty bore Bo Xin, Prince of Hengyang. Lady Wang the Filling Beauty bore Bo Ren, Prince of Luling. Lady Zhang the Cultivated Beauty bore Bo Yi, Prince of Jiangxia. Lady Han the Cultivated Beauty bore Bo Li, Prince of Wuling. Lady Jiang the Honored Consort bore Bo Zhi, Prince of Yongyang. Lady Kong the Honored Consort bore Bo Mou, Prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 其伯固犯逆別有傳。

translations.literal: Bo Gu's rebellion is treated in a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Gu's rebellion is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 二男早卒，本書無名。

translations.literal: Two sons died young; this book gives no names.
translations.idiomatic: Two sons died young; this book gives no names.

sentences.zh: 始興王伯茂字鬱之，世祖第二子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shixing Bo Mao, styled Yuzhi, was Emperor Wen's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Mao, Prince of Shixing, styled Yuzhi, was Emperor Wen's second son.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖兄始興昭烈王道談仕於梁世，為東宮直閤將軍，侯景之亂，領弩手二千援臺，於城中中流矢卒。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Founder's elder brother Prince Zhaolie of Shixing Dao Tan had served in Liang times as Direct Attendant of the Eastern Palace; in Hou Jing's rebellion he led two thousand crossbowmen to relieve the capital and died in the city from an arrow wound.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Founder's elder brother Dao Tan, Prince Zhaolie of Shixing, had served in Liang as direct attendant of the eastern palace. In Hou Jing's rebellion he led two thousand crossbowmen to relieve the capital and was killed in the city by an arrow.

sentences.zh: （紹泰）

translations.literal: Collation variant: Shaotai.
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: Shaotai.

sentences.zh: 〔太平〕二年，追贈侍中、使持節、都督南兗州諸軍事、南兗州刺史，封

translations.literal: Collation variant: [Taiping]; second year, posthumously promoted to Palace Attendant, bearer of the staff with equal court ceremony to the Three Dukes, commander of all military affairs in South Yanzhou and inspector of South Yanzhou, and enfeoffed as
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: [Taiping]; second year, posthumously made palace attendant, bearer of the staff with equal court ceremony to the three dukes, commander of all military affairs in South Yanzhou and inspector of South Yanzhou, and enfeoffed as

sentences.zh: （義興郡公）

translations.literal: (Yixing Commandery Duke).
translations.idiomatic: (Yixing Commandery Duke).

sentences.zh: 〔長城縣公〕，〔一〕諡曰昭烈。

translations.literal: [Changcheng County Duke], Editorial footnote marker 1. with posthumous title Zhaolie.
translations.idiomatic: [Changcheng County Duke], [1] with posthumous title Zhaolie.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，重贈驃騎大將軍、太傅、〔二〕揚州牧，改封始興郡王，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, he again posthumously promoted him to Cavalry General-in-Chief, Grand Tutor, Editorial footnote marker 2. Governor of Yangzhou, changed the enfeoffment to Prince of Shixing Commandery, fief two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, he again posthumously made him cavalry general-in-chief and grand tutor, [2] governor of Yangzhou, and changed the fief to Prince of Shixing, two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 王生世祖及高宗。

translations.literal: The prince was father to Emperor Wen and Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was father to Emperor Wen and Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 高宗以梁承聖末遷于關右，至是高祖遙以高宗襲封始興嗣王，以奉昭烈王祀。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan had moved to the Guanzhong region at the end of Liang's Chengsheng era; by then the Founder remotely had Emperor Xuan inherit the fief as heir Prince of Shixing to maintain sacrifice to Prince Zhaolie.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan had gone west to Guanzhong at the end of Liang's Chengsheng era. The Founder then had him inherit remotely as heir Prince of Shixing to maintain sacrifice to Prince Zhaolie.

sentences.zh: 永定三年六月，高祖崩，是月世祖入纂帝位。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Yongding year 3 the Founder died; that month Emperor Wen entered to succeed the imperial line.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Yongding year 3 (559) the Founder died; that month Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時高宗在周未還，世祖以本宗乏饗，其年十月下詔曰：「日者皇基肇建，封樹枝戚，朕親地攸在，特啟大邦。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xuan was still in Zhou and had not returned; Emperor Wen, because the main line lacked offerings, in the tenth month of that year issued an edict saying: "Of late the imperial foundation was first laid and fiefs and branches were planted; my own domain lies here, and a great state was opened especially for me.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was still in Zhou and had not returned. Because the main line lacked offerings, in the tenth month of that year Emperor Wen issued an edict: "Of late the imperial foundation was laid and fiefs planted for kin; my own domain lies here, and a great state was opened especially for me.

sentences.zh: 弟頊嗣承門祀，雖土宇開建，薦饗莫由。

translations.literal: My younger brother Xu inherits and carries on the house sacrifices; though his territory was established, he has no means to offer them.
translations.idiomatic: My younger brother Xu inherits the house sacrifices; though his territory was established, he has no means to offer them.

sentences.zh: 重以遭家不造，閔凶夙遘，儲貳遐隔，轊車未返。

translations.literal: Moreover our house met misfortune; mourning came early; the heir was far away and the returning carriage had not come back.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover our house met misfortune and mourning came early; the heir was far away and the returning carriage had not come back.

sentences.zh: 猥以眇身，膺茲景命，式循龜鼎，冰谷載懷。

translations.literal: I unworthily with this slight person received this bright mandate, following the tortoise and tripod, my heart laden as on ice in a valley.
translations.idiomatic: I unworthily with this slight person received this bright mandate, following the tortoise and tripod, my heart laden as on ice in a valley.

sentences.zh: 今既入奉大宗，事絕藩祼，始興國廟蒸嘗無主，瞻言霜露，感尋慟絕。

translations.literal: Now that I have entered to serve the great lineage, the matter of princely libation is ended; the Shixing state temple has no one for its seasonal offerings—gazing on the frost and dew, I am moved to grief and anguish.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have entered to serve the great lineage, princely libation is ended; the Shixing state temple has no one for its seasonal offerings. Gazing on frost and dew, I am moved to grief and anguish.

sentences.zh: 其徙封嗣王頊為安成王，封第二子伯茂為始興王，以奉昭烈王祀。

translations.literal: The heir Prince Xu is to be moved in fief to Prince of Ancheng; the second son Bo Mao is to be enfeoffed Prince of Shixing to maintain sacrifice to Prince Zhaolie.
translations.idiomatic: The heir Prince Xu is to be moved in fief to Prince of Ancheng; the second son Bo Mao is to be enfeoffed Prince of Shixing to maintain sacrifice to Prince Zhaolie.

sentences.zh: 賜天下為父後者爵一級。

translations.literal: Grant throughout the realm one rank of nobility to those who are heirs to their fathers.
translations.idiomatic: Grant throughout the realm one rank of nobility to those who are heirs to their fathers.

sentences.zh: 庶申罔極之情，永保山河之祚。」

translations.literal: Thus may boundless feeling be expressed and the mountains and rivers forever secured in blessing."
translations.idiomatic: Thus may boundless feeling be expressed and the mountains and rivers forever secured in blessing."

sentences.zh: 舊制諸王受封，未加戎號者，不置佐史，於是尚書八座奏曰：「 夫增崇徽號，飾表車服，所以闡彰厥德，下變民望。

translations.literal: By old regulation when princes received enfeoffment, if they had not yet been given military titles they were not provided staff clerks; thereupon the eight seats of the Masters of Writing memorialized: "To increase and exalt emblematic titles and adorn carriage and dress is to make manifest their virtue and transform the people's expectations below.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation, when princes received enfeoffment without a military title they were not given staff clerks. The eight seats of the Masters of Writing memorialized: "To increase emblematic titles and adorn carriage and dress is to manifest virtue and transform the people's expectations below.

sentences.zh: 第二皇子新除始興王伯茂，體自尊極，神姿明穎，玉映戮辰，蘭芬綺歲，清暉美譽，日茂月升，道鬱平、河，聲超袞、植。

translations.literal: The second prince, newly invested Prince of Shixing Bo Mao, in person honors the utmost pole, his spirit bright and keen; jade reflects at the killing hour, orchid fragrance at brocade years; pure splendor and fine reputation daily flourish and monthly rise; the Way is rich as Ping and He, his fame surpasses Gun and Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The second prince, newly invested Bo Mao, Prince of Shixing, in person honors the utmost pole; his spirit is bright and keen, jade reflects at the killing hour, orchid fragrance at brocade years; pure splendor and fine reputation daily flourish; the Way is rich as Ping and He, his fame surpasses Gun and Zhi.

sentences.zh: 皇情追感，聖性天深，以本宗闕緒，纂承藩嗣，雖珪社是膺，而戎章未襲，豈所以光崇睿哲，寵樹皇枝。

translations.literal: The imperial feeling pursues remembrance; sagely nature is heaven-deep; because the main line lacked succession he inherits and carries on the princely heir—though he received the jade and altars, his military patent was not conferred; how could this glorify sagely wisdom and favor the imperial branches?
translations.idiomatic: The imperial feeling pursues remembrance; sagely nature is heaven-deep. Because the main line lacked succession he inherits the princely heir—though he received jade and altars, his military patent was not conferred. How could this glorify sagely wisdom and favor the imperial branches?

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，宜加寧遠將軍，置佐史。

translations.literal: We your subjects deliberated: he should be given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distant and provided staff clerks.
translations.idiomatic: We your subjects deliberated: he should be given the additional title general who pacifies the distant and provided staff clerks.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰「可」。

translations.literal: The edict said, "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "Approved."

sentences.zh: 尋除使持節、都督南琅邪彭城二郡諸軍事、彭城太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was made bearer of the staff, commander of all military affairs in the two commanderies of South Langye and Pengcheng, and administrator of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made bearer of the staff, commander of all military affairs in South Langye and Pengcheng, and administrator of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 天嘉二年，進號宣惠將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In Tianjia year 2 his title was advanced to General Who Proclaims Favor and inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 2 (561) his title was advanced to general who proclaims favor and inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 伯茂性聰敏，好學，謙恭下士，又以太子母弟，世祖深愛重之。

translations.literal: Bo Mao was clever and keen by nature, loved learning, was modest and respectful to men of worth, and because he was the crown prince's younger brother by the same mother Emperor Wen cherished him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Mao was clever and keen by nature, loved learning, and was modest and respectful to men of worth. Because he was the crown prince's younger brother by the same mother, Emperor Wen cherished him deeply.

sentences.zh: 是時征北軍人於丹徒盜發晉郗曇墓，大獲晉右將軍王羲之書及諸名賢遺跡。

translations.literal: At that time soldiers of the campaign-north army at Dantu illicitly opened the Jin tomb of Xi Tan and greatly obtained writings of Jin's Right General Wang Xizhi and traces of various famous worthies.
translations.idiomatic: At that time soldiers of the campaign-north army at Dantu illicitly opened the Jin tomb of Xi Tan and greatly obtained writings of Jin's right general Wang Xizhi and traces of various famous worthies.

sentences.zh: 事覺，其書並沒縣官，藏于祕府，世祖以伯茂好古，多以賜之，由是伯茂大工草隸，甚得右軍之法。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light the writings were all confiscated to the county office and stored in the secret repository; Emperor Wen, because Bo Mao loved antiquity, gave many to him; thereby Bo Mao became highly skilled in cursive and clerical script and thoroughly obtained the Right General's method.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter came to light the writings were confiscated to the county office and stored in the secret repository. Because Bo Mao loved antiquity, Emperor Wen gave many to him; thereby Bo Mao became highly skilled in cursive and clerical script and thoroughly obtained the Right General's method.

sentences.zh: 三年，除鎮東將軍、開府儀同三司、東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In year 3 he was made General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master with Ceremonial Parity to the Three Offices, and inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was made general who pacifies the east, grand master with ceremonial parity to the three offices, and inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，時伯茂在都，劉師知等矯詔出高宗也，伯茂勸成之。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor ascended, Bo Mao was then in the capital; Liu Shizhi and others forged an edict to send out Emperor Xuan, and Bo Mao urged it to success.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor ascended, Bo Mao was in the capital. Liu Shizhi and others forged an edict to send out Emperor Xuan, and Bo Mao urged it to success.

sentences.zh: 師知等誅後，高宗恐伯茂扇動朝廷，光大元年，乃進號中衛將軍，令入居禁中，專與廢帝遊處。

translations.literal: After Shizhi and the rest were executed, Emperor Xuan feared Bo Mao would stir the court; in Guangda year 1 he advanced his title to General of the Central Guard and ordered him to live within the forbidden quarters, exclusively associating with the Deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizhi and the rest were executed, Emperor Xuan feared Bo Mao would stir the court. In Guangda year 1 (567) he advanced his title to general of the central guard and ordered him to live within the forbidden quarters, exclusively associating with the Deposed Emperor.

sentences.zh: 是時四海之望，咸歸高宗，伯茂深不平，日夕憤怨，數肆惡言，高宗以其無能，不以為意。

translations.literal: At that time the hopes of all within the seas turned to Emperor Xuan; Bo Mao was deeply discontent, day and night resentful, and repeatedly uttered vicious words; Emperor Xuan, because he was incapable, did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the hopes of all within the seas turned to Emperor Xuan. Bo Mao was deeply discontent, day and night resentful, and repeatedly uttered vicious words. Emperor Xuan, because he was incapable, did not take it to heart.

sentences.zh: 及建安人蔣裕與韓子高等謀反，伯茂並陰豫其事。

translations.literal: When the man of Jian'an Jiang Yu plotted rebellion with Han Zigao and others, Bo Mao also secretly took part in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Yu of Jian'an plotted rebellion with Han Zigao and others, Bo Mao also secretly took part.

sentences.zh: 二年十一月，皇太后令黜廢帝為臨海王，其日又下令曰：「伯茂輕薄，爰自弱齡，辜負嚴訓，彌肆凶狡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of year 2 the Empress Dowager ordered the Deposed Emperor demoted to Prince of Linhai; that same day she also issued an order: "Bo Mao is frivolous; from his tender years he has failed stern instruction and ever more indulged fierce cunning.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 2 the empress dowager ordered the Deposed Emperor demoted to Prince of Linhai. That same day she also issued an order: "Bo Mao is frivolous. From his tender years he has failed stern instruction and ever more indulged fierce cunning.

sentences.zh: 常以次居介弟，宜秉國權，不涯年德，逾逞狂躁，圖為禍亂，扇動宮闈，要招麤險，觖望臺閣，嗣君喪道，由此亂階，是諸凶德，咸作謀主。

translations.literal: Constantly by order of birth the younger brother next in line, he ought to hold state power; without limit to years and virtue he overstepped into wild arrogance, plotting disorder, stirring the palace apartments, summoning coarse danger, coveting the terrace offices; the heir lost the Way—hence this path of chaos; of all these vicious qualities he was chief plotter.
translations.idiomatic: Constantly by order of birth the younger brother next in line, he ought to hold state power. Without limit to years and virtue he overstepped into wild arrogance, plotting disorder, stirring the palace apartments, summoning coarse danger, coveting the terrace offices. The heir lost the Way—hence this path of chaos. Of all these vicious qualities he was chief plotter.

sentences.zh: 允宜罄彼司甸，刑斯剭人。

translations.literal: He should indeed be exhausted in that judicial district and this violent man punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: He should indeed be exhausted in that judicial district and this violent man punished by law.

sentences.zh: 言念皇支，尚懷悲懣，可特降為溫麻侯，宜加禁止，別遣就第。

translations.literal: Speaking of the imperial branches, I still harbor grief and anger; he is specially demoted to Marquis of Wenma; he should be placed under restraint and separately sent to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of the imperial branches, I still harbor grief and anger. He is specially demoted to Marquis of Wenma, placed under restraint, and separately sent to his residence.

sentences.zh: 不意如此，言增泫歎。

translations.literal: I did not expect this—my words increase in weeping and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect this—my words increase in weeping and sighing.

sentences.zh: 」時六門之外有別館，以為諸王冠婚之所，名為婚第，至是命伯茂出居之。

translations.literal: Outside the Six Gates there was a separate lodge used as the place where princes received caps and married, called the Marriage Lodge; at this time Bo Mao was ordered to go out and dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Six Gates there was a separate lodge where princes received caps and married, called the Marriage Lodge. At this time Bo Mao was ordered to go out and dwell there.

sentences.zh: 於路遇盜，殞于車中，時年十八。

translations.literal: On the road he met bandits and perished in the carriage; he was eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he met bandits and perished in the carriage. He was eighteen.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽王伯山字靜之，世祖第三子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Poyang Bo Shan, styled Jingzhi, was Emperor Wen's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Shan, Prince of Poyang, styled Jingzhi, was Emperor Wen's third son.

sentences.zh: 偉容儀，舉止閑雅，喜慍不形於色，世祖深器之。

translations.literal: His appearance was imposing; his bearing leisurely and elegant; pleasure and anger did not show on his face; Emperor Wen deeply valued him.
translations.idiomatic: His appearance was imposing; his bearing leisurely and elegant; pleasure and anger did not show on his face. Emperor Wen deeply valued him.

sentences.zh: 初高祖時，天下草創，諸王受封儀注多闕，及伯山受封，世祖欲重其事，天嘉元年七月丙辰，尚書八座奏曰：「臣聞本枝惟允，宗周之業以弘，盤石既建，皇漢之基斯遠，故能協宣五運，規範百王，式固靈根，克隆卜世。

translations.literal: In the Founder's time the realm was newly founded and the ritual and regulations for princes receiving enfeoffment were largely lacking; when Bo Shan received enfeoffment Emperor Wen wished to make the affair weighty; in the seventh month of Tianjia year 1, on bingchen, the eight seats of the Masters of Writing memorialized: "Your subject has heard that the root branch must be secure and the Zhou house's enterprise thereby enlarged; the bedrock boulder once set, the Han foundation thereby far-reaching—thus they could harmonize and proclaim the five cycles and regulate the hundred kings, firmly securing the numinous root and cloning fortune for generations.
translations.idiomatic: In the Founder's time the realm was newly founded and ritual for princes receiving enfeoffment was largely lacking. When Bo Shan received enfeoffment Emperor Wen wished to make the affair weighty. In the seventh month of Tianjia year 1 (560), on bingchen, the eight seats memorialized: "We have heard that the root branch must be secure and the Zhou house's enterprise thereby enlarged; the bedrock boulder once set, the Han foundation thereby far-reaching—thus they could harmonize the five cycles and regulate the hundred kings, firmly securing the numinous root and cloning fortune for generations.

sentences.zh: 第三皇子伯山，發睿德於齠年，表歧姿於丱日，光昭丹掖，暉映青闈，而玉圭未秉，金錫靡駕，豈所以敦序維翰，建樹藩戚。

translations.literal: The third prince Bo Shan displayed sagely virtue in his tender years and showed a singular bearing in his cap years; brilliance shone in the cinnabar side-chamber and radiance in the blue inner gate—yet the jade tablet was not held and gold and tin were not harnessed; how could this be ordering the great branches and establishing the princely kin?
translations.idiomatic: The third prince Bo Shan displayed sagely virtue in his tender years and a singular bearing in his cap years; brilliance shone in the cinnabar side-chamber and radiance in the blue inner gate—yet the jade tablet was not held and gold and tin were not harnessed. How could this order the great branches and establish princely kin?

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，宜封鄱陽郡王。

translations.literal: We your subjects deliberated: he should be enfeoffed Prince of Poyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: We your subjects deliberated: he should be enfeoffed Prince of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰「可」。

translations.literal: The edict said, "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "Approved."

sentences.zh: 乃遣散騎常侍、度支尚書蕭睿持節兼太宰告于太廟；

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Attendant Cavalier at Large and Commissioner of Revenue Xiao Rui bearing the staff concurrently as Grand Mentor to announce at the Imperial Temple;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he sent attendant cavalier at large and commissioner of revenue Xiao Rui bearing the staff concurrently as grand mentor to announce at the Imperial Temple;

sentences.zh: 又遣五兵尚書王質持節兼太宰告于太社。

translations.literal: he also sent Master of the Five Armaments Wang Zhi bearing the staff concurrently as Grand Mentor to announce at the Altar of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: he also sent master of the five armaments Wang Zhi bearing the staff concurrently as grand mentor to announce at the Altar of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，上臨軒策命之曰：「於戲！

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year the emperor came to the hall to bestow the investiture mandate, saying: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year the emperor came to the hall to bestow the investiture mandate, saying: "Alas!

sentences.zh: 夫建樹藩屏，翼獎王室，欽若前典，咸必由之。

translations.literal: To establish the princely screen and assist and reward the royal house—reverently following the former canon, all must pass through this.
translations.idiomatic: To establish the princely screen and assist and reward the royal house—reverently following the former canon, all must pass through this.

sentences.zh: 惟爾夙挺珪璋，生知孝敬，〔三〕令德茂親，僉譽所集，啟建大邦，寔惟倫序，是用敬遵民瞻，錫此圭瑞。

translations.literal: You from youth have stood forth like jade and scepter, born knowing filial respect; Editorial footnote marker 3. your fine virtue enriches kinship, the unanimous praise of the gathered; to open a great state is truly the proper order of human relations—therefore I reverently follow the people's gaze and grant this jade and investiture.
translations.idiomatic: You from youth have stood forth like jade and scepter, born knowing filial respect; [3] your fine virtue enriches kinship, unanimous praise of the gathered. To open a great state is truly the proper order of human relations—therefore I reverently follow the people's gaze and grant this jade and investiture.

sentences.zh: 往欽哉！

translations.literal: Go—be reverent!
translations.idiomatic: Go—be reverent!

sentences.zh: 其勉樹聲業，永保宗社，可不慎歟！

translations.literal: Strive to build your reputation and forever secure the ancestral altars—can you not be cautious?"
translations.idiomatic: Strive to build your reputation and forever secure the ancestral altars—can you not be cautious?"

sentences.zh: 」策訖，敕令王公已下並醼於王第。

translations.literal: When the mandate was finished he ordered princes and dukes and below all to feast at the prince's residence.
translations.idiomatic: When the mandate was finished he ordered princes, dukes, and below all to feast at the prince's residence.

sentences.zh: 仍授東中郎將、吳郡太守。

translations.literal: He was then made General of the Eastern Center and administrator of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made general of the eastern center and administrator of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 六年，為緣江都督、平北將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In year 6 he was made commander along the river, General Who Pacifies the North, and inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was made commander along the river, general who pacifies the north, and inspector of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 天康元年，進號鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: In Tiankang year 1 his title was advanced to General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiankang year 1 (566) his title was advanced to general who guards the north.

sentences.zh: 長子君範，太建中拜鄱陽國世子，尋為貞威將軍、晉陵太守，未襲爵而隋師至。

translations.literal: His eldest son Junfan, in the Taijian era was invested heir of the Poyang state; soon he was made General of Manifest Prestige and administrator of Jinling; before he could inherit the title the Sui army arrived.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Junfan, in the Taijian era was invested heir of the Poyang state; soon he was made general of manifest prestige and administrator of Jinling. Before he could inherit the title the Sui army arrived.

sentences.zh: 是時宗室王侯在都者百餘人，後主恐其為變，乃並召入，令屯朝堂，使豫章王叔英總督之，而又陰為之備。

translations.literal: At that time more than a hundred princes of the imperial house in the capital were there; Houzhu feared they would make trouble and summoned them all in, ordering them to encamp at the Court Hall and putting the Prince of Yuzhang Chen Shuying in overall command, while also secretly making preparations.
translations.idiomatic: At that time more than a hundred princes of the imperial house were in the capital. Houzhu feared they would make trouble, summoned them all in, ordered them to encamp at the Court Hall, and put Chen Shuying, Prince of Yuzhang, in overall command, while also secretly making preparations.

sentences.zh: 及六軍敗績，相率出降，因從後主入關。

translations.literal: When the six armies were defeated they went out in succession to surrender and followed Houzhu into the passes.
translations.idiomatic: When the six armies were defeated they went out in succession to surrender and followed Houzhu into the passes.

sentences.zh: 至長安，隋文帝並配于隴右及河西諸州，各給田業以處之。

translations.literal: Reaching Chang'an, Emperor Wen of Sui assigned them all to Longyou and the commanderies west of the river, each given fields and estates for settlement.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Chang'an, Emperor Wen of Sui assigned them all to Longyou and the commanderies west of the river, each given fields and estates for settlement.

sentences.zh: 初，君範與尚書僕射江總友善，至是總贈君範書五言詩，以敘他鄉離別之意，辭甚酸切，當世文士咸諷誦之。

translations.literal: Earlier Junfan had been friendly with Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Jiang Zong; at this time Zong presented Junfan a pentasyllabic poem expressing the feeling of parting in another land—the words very bitter and keen; the literary men of the age all chanted and recited it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Junfan had been friendly with vice director of the masters of writing Jiang Zong. At this time Zong presented Junfan a pentasyllabic poem expressing parting in another land—the words very bitter and keen; the literary men of the age all chanted and recited it.

sentences.zh: 大業二年，隋煬帝以後主第六女女婤為貴人，絕愛幸，因召陳氏子弟盡還京師，隨才敘用，由是並為守宰，遍於天下。

translations.literal: In Daye year 2 Emperor Yang of Sui took Houzhu's sixth daughter Nüyao as honored consort and loved her exceedingly; he therefore summoned the Chen clan's younger kinsmen all back to the capital and employed them according to talent—thereby they all became prefects and magistrates throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year 2 (606) Emperor Yang of Sui took Houzhu's sixth daughter Nüyao as honored consort and loved her exceedingly. He therefore summoned the Chen clan's younger kinsmen all back to the capital and employed them according to talent—thereby they all became prefects and magistrates throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 其年君範為溫令。

translations.literal: That year Junfan was made magistrate of Wen.
translations.idiomatic: That year Junfan was made magistrate of Wen.

sentences.zh: 衡陽王伯信字孚之，世祖第七子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hengyang Bo Xin, styled Fuzhi, was Emperor Wen's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Xin, Prince of Hengyang, styled Fuzhi, was Emperor Wen's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，衡陽獻王昌自周還朝，於道薨，其年世祖立伯信為衡陽王，奉獻王祀。

translations.literal: In Tianjia year 1 Prince Xian of Hengyang Chang returned from Zhou to court and died on the road; that year Emperor Wen installed Bo Xin as Prince of Hengyang to maintain sacrifice to the Xian prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 1 (560) Prince Xian of Hengyang Chang returned from Zhou to court and died on the road. That year Emperor Wen installed Bo Xin as Prince of Hengyang to maintain sacrifice to the Xian prince.

sentences.zh: 尋為宣惠將軍、丹陽尹，置佐史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made General Who Proclaims Favor and governor of Danyang, with staff clerks provided.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made general who proclaims favor and governor of Danyang, with staff clerks provided.

sentences.zh: 太建四年，為中護軍。

translations.literal: In Taijian year 4 he was made General of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 4 (572) he was made general of the central guard.

sentences.zh: 六年，為宣毅將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In year 6 he was made General Who Proclaims Resolution and inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 (574) he was made general who proclaims resolution and inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋加侍中、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional posts of Palace Attendant and Attendant Cavalier at Large.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the additional posts of palace attendant and attendant cavalier at large.

sentences.zh: 十一年，進號鎮前將軍，〔六〕太子詹事，餘並如故。

translations.literal: In year 11 his title was advanced to General Who Guards the Front, Editorial footnote marker 6. Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent, the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 (579) his title was advanced to general who guards the front, [6] grand mentor to the heir apparent, the rest as before.

sentences.zh: 禎明元年，出為鎮南將軍、西衡州刺史。

translations.literal: In Zhenming year 1 he went out as General Who Guards the South and inspector of Western Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 1 (587) he went out as general who guards the south and inspector of Western Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，隋軍濟江，與臨汝侯方慶並為東衡州刺史王勇所害，〔七〕事在方慶傳。

translations.literal: In year 3 when the Sui army crossed the river he and the Marquis of Linru Fang Qing were both killed by Eastern Hengzhou inspector Wang Yong, Editorial footnote marker 7. treated in Fang Qing's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 (589), when the Sui army crossed the river, he and the Marquis of Linru Fang Qing were both killed by Eastern Hengzhou inspector Wang Yong, [7] treated in Fang Qing's biography.

sentences.zh: 廬陵王伯仁字壽之，世祖第八子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Luling Bo Ren, styled Shouzhi, was Emperor Wen's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Ren, Prince of Luling, styled Shouzhi, was Emperor Wen's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 天嘉六年，立為廬陵王。

translations.literal: In Tianjia year 6 he was installed as Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 6 (565) he was installed as Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 太建初，為輕車將軍，置佐史。

translations.literal: At the opening of Taijian he was made General of the Light Chariot, with staff clerks provided.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taijian he was made general of the light chariot, with staff clerks provided.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷冠軍將軍、中領軍。

translations.literal: In year 7 he was transferred to General Who Exerts Might and General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 (575) he was transferred to general who exerts might and general of the central army.

sentences.zh: 〔八〕尋為平北將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 8. Soon he was made General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: [8] Soon he was made general who pacifies the north and inspector of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二年，為翊左將軍、中領軍。

translations.literal: In year 12 he was made General of the Left Wing and General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 (580) he was made general of the left wing and general of the central army.

sentences.zh: 禎明元年，加侍中、〔九〕國子祭酒，領太子中庶子。

translations.literal: In Zhenming year 1 he was given the additional posts of Palace Attendant, Editorial footnote marker 9. Libationer of the National University, and concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 1 he was given the additional posts of palace attendant, [9] libationer of the National University, and concurrently supervisor of the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 三年入關，卒于長安。

translations.literal: In year 3 he entered the passes and died at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he entered the passes and died at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 長子番，先封湘濱侯，隋大業中，為資陽令。

translations.literal: His eldest son Fan had earlier been enfeoffed Marquis of Xiangbin; in Sui's Daye era he was magistrate of Ziyang.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Fan had earlier been enfeoffed Marquis of Xiangbin. In Sui's Daye era he was magistrate of Ziyang.

sentences.zh: 江夏王伯義字堅之，世祖第九子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jiangxia Bo Yi, styled Jianzhi, was Emperor Wen's ninth son.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Yi, Prince of Jiangxia, styled Jianzhi, was Emperor Wen's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 天嘉六年，立為江夏王。

translations.literal: In Tianjia year 6 he was installed as Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 6 he was installed as Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 太建初，為宣惠將軍、東揚州刺史，置佐史。

translations.literal: At the opening of Taijian he was made General Who Proclaims Favor and inspector of Eastern Yangzhou, with staff clerks provided.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taijian he was made general who proclaims favor and inspector of Eastern Yangzhou, with staff clerks provided.

sentences.zh: 尋為宣毅將軍、持節、散騎常侍、都督合霍二州諸軍事、合州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made General Who Proclaims Resolution, bearer of the staff, Attendant Cavalier at Large, commander of all military affairs in the two prefectures of He and Huo, and inspector of He.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made general who proclaims resolution, bearer of the staff, attendant cavalier at large, commander of all military affairs in He and Huo, and inspector of He.

sentences.zh: 〔一０〕十四年，徵為侍中、忠武將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 10. In year 14 he was summoned as Palace Attendant, General of Loyal Martiality, and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: [10] In year 14 (582) he was summoned as palace attendant, general of loyal martiality, and grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年入關，遷于瓜州，於道卒。

translations.literal: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the passes, was moved to Guazhou, and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the passes, was moved to Guazhou, and died on the road.

sentences.zh: 長子元基，先封湘潭侯，隋大業中為穀熟縣令。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yuanji had earlier been enfeoffed Marquis of Xiangtan; in Sui's Daye era he was magistrate of Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yuanji had earlier been enfeoffed Marquis of Xiangtan. In Sui's Daye era he was magistrate of Gushu.

sentences.zh: 武陵王伯禮字用之，世祖第十子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wuling Bo Li, styled Yongzhi, was Emperor Wen's tenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Li, Prince of Wuling, styled Yongzhi, was Emperor Wen's tenth son.

sentences.zh: 天嘉六年，立為武陵王。

translations.literal: In Tianjia year 6 he was installed as Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 6 he was installed as Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 太建初，為雲旗將軍、持節、都督吳興諸軍事、吳興太守。

translations.literal: At the opening of Taijian he was made General of the Cloud Banner, bearer of the staff, commander of all military affairs in Wuxing, and administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taijian he was made general of the cloud banner, bearer of the staff, commander of all military affairs in Wuxing, and administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 在郡恣行暴掠，驅錄民下，逼奪財貨，前後委積，百姓患之。

translations.literal: In the commandery he wantonly committed violence and plunder, driving and registering the people below, forcing seizure of goods—before and after they piled up; the common people suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he wantonly committed violence and plunder, driving and registering the people, forcing seizure of goods until they piled up; the common people suffered.

sentences.zh: 太建九年，為有司所劾，上曰王年少，未達治道，皆由佐史不能匡弼所致，特降軍號，後若更犯，必致之以法，有司不言與同罪。

translations.literal: In Taijian year 9 he was impeached by the relevant office; the emperor said the prince was young and had not yet attained the way of governance—it was all because the staff clerks could not correct and assist him; his military title was specially lowered; if hereafter he again offended, he would certainly be brought to law; if the relevant office did not speak up they would share the crime.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 9 (577) he was impeached by the relevant office. The emperor said the prince was young and had not yet attained the way of governance—it was all because the staff clerks could not correct and assist him. His military title was specially lowered; if hereafter he again offended, he would certainly be brought to law; if the relevant office did not speak up they would share the crime.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，被代徵還，伯禮遂遷延不發。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year he was replaced and summoned back; Boli thereupon delayed and would not depart.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year he was relieved and summoned home, but Boli delayed and would not set out.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，散騎常侍、御史中丞徐君敷奏曰：〔一一〕「臣聞車屨不俟，君命之通規，夙夜匪懈，臣子之恆節。

translations.literal: That year, in the tenth month, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Censor-in-Chief Xu Junfu memorialized, saying: "Your servant has heard that one does not await the carriage and boots—this is the general rule for a lord's command; to rise early and never slacken is the constant duty of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the tenth month, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and censor-in-chief Xu Junfu memorialized: "I have heard that one does not await carriage and boots—such is the rule of a lord's command; rising early and never slackening is a minister's constant duty.

sentences.zh: 謹案雲旗將軍、持節、都督吳興諸軍事、吳興太守武陵王伯禮，早擅英猷〔一二〕，久馳令問，惟良寄重，枌鄉是屬。

translations.literal: I respectfully report on Cloud-Banner General, Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Wuxing Military Affairs and Administrator of Wuxing, the Prince of Wuling, Boli: from early on he excelled in fine plans, long bore an excellent reputation, was entrusted as the worthy man, and his native district was his charge.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully report on cloud-banner general, bearer of the staff, commander-in-chief of Wuxing military affairs and administrator of Wuxing, Prince of Wuling Boli: from early on he excelled in counsel and long bore a fine reputation; the realm entrusted him and his native district was his charge.

sentences.zh: 聖上愛育黔黎，留情政本，共化求瘼，早赴皇心，遂復稽緩歸驂，取移敘燠，遲回去鷁，空淹載路，淑慎未彰，違惰斯在，繩愆檢跡，以為懲誡。

translations.literal: His Majesty cherishes and nurtures the black-haired people and keeps his mind on the root of government, seeking together to relieve suffering and soon meeting the imperial heart—yet he again was slow in returning his carriage-team, shifting the season of warmth, delaying his homeward sails, vainly lingering on the road. Gentle caution was not shown; disobedience and sloth were present. To bind faults and examine traces is fitting as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty cherishes the people and keeps his mind on government, seeking together to relieve suffering as the throne wished—yet he again delayed his return, shifting the season's warmth, lingering on the road with homeward sails belated. Gentle caution went unshown; sloth and disobedience stood plain. Faults must be bound and traces examined as a warning.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議以見事免伯禮所居官，以王還第，謹以白簡奏聞。

translations.literal: We your servants jointly propose that, on the present case, Boli be removed from the offices he holds, that he return to his princely residence, and we respectfully submit this white memorandum for report.
translations.idiomatic: We jointly propose that on the present case Boli be removed from office, sent back to his residence, and we respectfully submit this report.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰「可」。

translations.literal: " An edict said, "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: " An edict said, "Approved."

sentences.zh: 禎明三年入關，隋大業中為散騎侍郎、臨洮太守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the Pass; in the Daye era of Sui he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Administrator of Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the Pass; under Sui's Daye era he served as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and administrator of Lintao.

sentences.zh: 永陽王伯智字策之，世祖第十二子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yongyang, Bozhi, styled Ce Zhi, was Emperor Wen's twelfth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Bozhi of Yongyang, styled Ce Zhi, was Emperor Wen's twelfth son.

sentences.zh: 少敦厚，有器局，博涉經史。

translations.literal: In youth he was steady and generous, had capacity and judgment, and read widely in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was steady and generous, with sound judgment, and read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 太建中，立為永陽王。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era he was established as Prince of Yongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taijian era he was made Prince of Yongyang.

sentences.zh: 〔一三〕尋為侍中，加明威將軍，置佐史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Brightly Martial General, with staff clerks appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made attendant-in-ordinary and brightly martial general, with staff clerks appointed.

sentences.zh: 尋加散騎常侍，累遷尚書左僕射，〔一四〕出為使持節、都督東揚豐二州諸軍事、〔一五〕平東將軍，領會稽內史。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and by successive promotions reached Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Dongyang and Feng Military Affairs, and Pacifying-East General, concurrently holding the post of Interior Minister of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and rose through posts to left vice director of the masters of writing; he went out as bearer of the staff, commander-in-chief of Dongyang and Feng military affairs, and pacifying-east general, concurrently interior minister of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，入為侍中、翊左將軍，加特進。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Assistant General, with special advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year 2 he entered court as attendant-in-ordinary and left assistant general, with special advancement.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年入關。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the Pass.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，為岐州司馬，遷國子司業。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he was made Vice Governor of Qi Prefecture, then promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui's Daye era he was vice governor of Qi prefecture, then promoted to vice director of the directorate of education.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王伯謀，字深之，世祖第十三子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guiyang, Bomou, styled Shen Zhi, was Emperor Wen's thirteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Bomou of Guiyang, styled Shen Zhi, was Emperor Wen's thirteenth son.

sentences.zh: 太建中，立為桂陽王。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era he was established as Prince of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taijian era he was made Prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 〔一六〕七年，為明威將軍，置佐史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was made Brightly Martial General, with staff clerks appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was made brightly martial general, with staff clerks appointed.

sentences.zh: 尋為信威將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Trustworthy Martial General and Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made trustworthy martial general and governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 十年，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was additionally Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he was additionally attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 出為持節、都督吳興諸軍事、東中郎將、吳興太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Wuxing Military Affairs, Eastern Central Commander-in-Chief, and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as bearer of the staff, commander-in-chief of Wuxing military affairs, eastern central commander-in-chief, and administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 十一年，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was additionally Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he was additionally regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 至德元年薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 he died.

sentences.zh: 子酆嗣，大業中，為番禾令。

translations.literal: His son Feng succeeded; in the Daye era he was made Magistrate of Fanhe.
translations.idiomatic: His son Feng succeeded; under the Daye era he was magistrate of Fanhe.

sentences.zh: 高宗四十二男：柳皇后生後主，彭貴人生始興王叔陵，曹淑華生豫章王叔英，何淑儀生長沙王叔堅、宜都王叔明，魏昭容生建安王叔卿，〔一七〕錢貴妃生河東王叔獻，劉昭儀生新蔡王叔齊，袁昭容生晉熙王叔文、義陽王叔達、新會王叔坦，王姬生淮南王叔彪、巴山王叔雄，〔一八〕吳姬生始興王叔重，徐姬生尋陽王叔儼，淳于姬生岳陽王叔慎，王脩華生武昌王叔虞，韋脩容生湘東王叔平，施姬生臨賀王叔敖、沅陵王叔興，曾姬生陽山王叔宣，楊姬生西陽王叔穆，申婕妤生南安王叔儉、南郡王叔澄、岳山王叔韶、太原王叔匡，袁姬生新興王叔純，吳姬生巴東王叔謨，劉姬生臨江王叔顯，〔一九〕秦姬生新寧王叔隆、新昌王叔榮。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan had forty-two sons: the Empress Liu bore Houzhu; Lady Peng bore the Prince of Shixing, Shuling; Lady Cao bore the Prince of Yuzhang, Shuying; Lady He bore the Prince of Changsha, Shujian, and the Prince of Yidu, Shuming; Lady Wei bore the Prince of Jian'an, Shuqing; Lady Qian bore the Prince of Hedong, Shuxian; Lady Liu bore the Prince of Xincai, Shuqi; Lady Yuan bore the Prince of Jinxi, Shuwen, the Prince of Yiyang, Shuda, and the Prince of Xinhui, Shutan; a Wang consort bore the Prince of Huainan, Shubiao, and the Prince of Bashan, Shuxiong; a Wu consort bore the Prince of Shixing, Shuzhong; Lady Xu bore the Prince of Xunyang, Shuyan; Lady Chunyu bore the Prince of Yueyang, Shushen; Lady Wang bore the Prince of Wuchang, Shuyu; Lady Wei bore the Prince of Xiangdong, Shuping; Lady Shi bore the Prince of Linhe, Shuao, and the Prince of Yuanling, Shuxing; Lady Zeng bore the Prince of Yangshan, Shuxuan; Lady Yang bore the Prince of Xiyang, Shumu; Lady Shen bore the Prince of Nan'an, Shujian, the Prince of Nanjun, Shucheng, the Prince of Yueshan, Shushao, and the Prince of Taiyuan, Shukuang; Lady Yuan bore the Prince of Xinxing, Shuchun; a Wu consort bore the Prince of Badong, Shumo; Lady Liu bore the Prince of Linjiang, Shuxian; Lady Qin bore the Prince of Xinning, Shulong, and the Prince of Xinchang, Shurong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan had forty-two sons: Empress Liu bore Houzhu; Lady Peng bore Prince Shuling of Shixing; Lady Cao bore Prince Shuying of Yuzhang; Lady He bore Prince Shujian of Changsha and Prince Shuming of Yidu; Lady Wei bore Prince Shuqing of Jian'an; Lady Qian bore Prince Shuqi of Xincai; Lady Yuan bore Prince Shuwen of Jinxi, Prince Shuda of Yiyang, and Prince Shutan of Xinhui; a Wang consort bore Prince Shubiao of Huainan and Prince Shuxiong of Bashan; a Wu consort bore Prince Shuzhong of Shixing; Lady Xu bore Prince Shuyan of Xunyang; Lady Chunyu bore Prince Shushen of Yueyang; Lady Wang bore Prince Shuyu of Wuchang; Lady Wei bore Prince Shuping of Xiangdong; Lady Shi bore Prince Shuao of Linhe and Prince Shuxing of Yuanling; Lady Zeng bore Prince Shuxuan of Yangshan; Lady Yang bore Prince Shumu of Xiyang; Lady Shen bore Prince Shujian of Nan'an, Prince Shucheng of Nanjun, Prince Shushao of Yueshan, and Prince Shukuang of Taiyuan; Lady Yuan bore Prince Shuchun of Xinxing; a Wu consort bore Prince Shumo of Badong; Lady Liu bore Prince Shuxian of Linjiang; Lady Qin bore Prince Shulong of Xinning and Prince Shurong of Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 其皇子叔叡、叔忠、叔

translations.literal: The imperial sons Shurui, Shuzhong, Shu
translations.idiomatic: The imperial sons Shurui, Shuzhong, Shu

translations.literal: (Yin)
translations.idiomatic: (Yin)

sentences.zh: 〔弘〕〔二０〕、叔毅、叔訓、叔武、叔處、叔封等八人，並未及封。

translations.literal: Hong, Shuyi, Shuxun, Shuwu, Shuchu, and Shufeng—eight men in all—had not yet been enfeoffed when the book was compiled.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, Shuyi, Shuxun, Shuwu, Shuchu, and Shufeng—eight in all—had not yet been enfeoffed when the book was compiled.

sentences.zh: 叔陵犯逆，別有傳。

translations.literal: Shuling's rebellion is treated in a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shuling's rebellion is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 三子早卒，本書無名。

translations.literal: Three sons died young; the original book gives no names.
translations.idiomatic: Three sons died young; the original book gives no names.

sentences.zh: 長子弘，至德元年，拜豫章國世子。

translations.literal: The eldest son Hong, in the first year of Zhide, was appointed heir of the state of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Hong, in Zhide year 1, was appointed heir of the state of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 長沙王叔堅字子成，高宗第四子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changsha, Shujian, styled Zicheng, was Emperor Xuan's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shujian of Changsha, styled Zicheng, was Emperor Xuan's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 母本吳中酒家隸，高宗微時，嘗往飲，遂與通，及貴，召拜淑儀。

translations.literal: His mother had originally been a wine-house servant girl in Wu; when Emperor Xuan was still obscure he once went to drink and consorted with her; when he rose high he summoned and appointed her Lady of Graceful Conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had been a wine-house servant in Wu; when Emperor Xuan was still obscure he once went drinking and took her; when he rose high he made her Lady of Graceful Conduct.

sentences.zh: 叔堅少傑黠，凶虐使酒，尤好數術、卜筮、祝禁，鎔金琢玉，並究其妙。

translations.literal: Shujian in youth was sharp and cunning, fierce and cruel, fond of wine, and especially loved numerology, divination, and talismanic prohibitions; smelting gold and carving jade—he pursued their subtleties to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Shujian in youth was sharp and cruel, fond of wine, and especially loved numerology, divination, and talismanic arts; smelting gold and carving jade—he pursued their subtleties to the end.

sentences.zh: 天嘉中，封豐城侯。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiancheng era he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，立為長沙王，仍為東中郎將、吳郡太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian he was established as Prince of Changsha and at the same time made Eastern Central Commander-in-Chief and Administrator of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 1 he was made Prince of Changsha and at the same time eastern central commander-in-chief and administrator of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 四年，為宣毅將軍、江州刺史，置佐史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made Pacifying-Assault General and Inspector of Jiangzhou, with staff clerks appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was made pacifying-assault general and inspector of Jiangzhou, with staff clerks appointed.

sentences.zh: 七年，進號雲麾將軍、郢州刺史，未拜，轉為平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was advanced to Cloud-Banner General and Inspector of Yingzhou; before he took up the post he was transferred to Pacifying-Yue Central Commander-in-Chief and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was advanced to cloud-banner general and inspector of Yingzhou; before taking up the post he was transferred to pacifying-yue central commander-in-chief and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋為平北將軍、合州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Pacifying-North General and Inspector of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made pacifying-north general and inspector of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 〔二五〕八年，復為平西將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was again made Pacifying-West General and Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was again made pacifying-west general and inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一年，入為翊左將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he entered court as Left Assistant General and Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he entered court as left assistant general and governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 〔二六〕

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 26.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 26.

sentences.zh: 初，叔堅與始興王叔陵並招聚賓客，各爭權寵，甚不平。

translations.literal: At first Shujian and the Prince of Shixing, Shuling, each gathered guests and vied for favor and power, deeply resenting one another.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shujian and Prince Shuling of Shixing each gathered clients and vied for favor, deeply resenting one another.

sentences.zh: 每朝會鹵簿，不肯為先後，必分道而趨，左右或爭道而鬥，至有死者。

translations.literal: Whenever at court assemblies the guard of honor would not yield precedence, they had to take separate roads and rush forward; attendants at times fought over the road, and there were even deaths.
translations.idiomatic: At court assemblies neither would yield precedence in the guard of honor; they took separate roads and rushed ahead, and attendants sometimes fought over the road—even to the death.

sentences.zh: 及高宗弗豫，叔堅、叔陵等並從後主侍疾。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan fell gravely ill, Shujian, Shuling, and the rest all attended Houzhu in nursing him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan fell gravely ill, Shujian, Shuling, and the rest all attended Houzhu at his bedside.

sentences.zh: 叔陵陰有異志，乃命典藥吏曰：「切藥刀甚鈍，可礪之。

translations.literal: Shuling harbored secret designs; he then ordered the pharmacy clerk, saying, "The medicine knife is very dull; it should be sharpened."
translations.idiomatic: Shuling harbored secret designs and ordered the pharmacy clerk, "The medicine knife is very dull; sharpen it."

sentences.zh: 」及高宗崩，倉卒之際，又命其左右於外取劍，左右弗悟，乃取朝服所佩木劍以進，叔陵怒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, in the haste of the moment he again ordered his attendants to fetch a sword from outside; the attendants did not understand and brought the wooden sword worn with court dress, and Shuling was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan died, in the haste of the moment he again ordered attendants to fetch a sword from outside; they did not understand and brought the wooden court sword, and Shuling was enraged.

sentences.zh: 叔堅在側聞之，疑有變，伺其所為。

translations.literal: Shujian, hearing this at his side, suspected trouble and watched what he would do.
translations.idiomatic: Shujian, hearing this beside him, suspected trouble and watched what he would do.

sentences.zh: 及翌日小斂，叔陵袖剉藥刀趨進，斫後主，中項，後主悶絕于地，皇太后與後主乳母樂安君吳氏俱以身捍之，獲免。

translations.literal: On the morrow, at the lesser encoffinment, Shuling hid a sharpened medicine knife in his sleeve, rushed forward, and hacked at Houzhu, striking the nape; Houzhu fainted to the ground. The Empress Dowager and Houzhu's wet-nurse, Lady Wu of Le'an, both used their bodies to shield him, and he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, at the lesser encoffinment, Shuling hid a sharpened medicine knife in his sleeve, rushed forward, and hacked at Houzhu, striking the nape; Houzhu fainted to the ground. The empress dowager and Houzhu's wet-nurse, Lady Wu of Le'an, both shielded him with their bodies, and he escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 叔堅自後扼叔陵，擒之，并奪其刀，將殺之，問後主曰：「即盡之，為待也。

translations.literal: Shujian from behind seized Shuling and captured him, also wresting away his knife; he was about to kill him and asked Houzhu, "Shall I finish him now, or wait?"
translations.idiomatic: Shujian seized Shuling from behind and captured him, wresting away his knife; he was about to kill him and asked Houzhu, "Shall I finish him now, or wait?"

sentences.zh: 」後主不能應。

translations.literal: Houzhu could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu could not answer.

sentences.zh: 叔陵舊多力，須臾，自奮得脫，出雲龍門，入于東府城，召左右斷青溪橋道，放東城囚以充戰士。

translations.literal: Shuling had long been very strong; in a moment he broke free by his own exertion, went out through the Cloud-Dragon Gate into the Eastern Palace city, summoned his attendants to cut the Qingxi Bridge road, and released prisoners from the eastern city to serve as fighting men.
translations.idiomatic: Shuling had long been very strong; in a moment he broke free, went out through the Cloud-Dragon Gate into the eastern palace city, summoned attendants to cut the Qingxi Bridge road, and released eastern-city prisoners to serve as fighting men.

sentences.zh: 又遣人往新林，追其所部兵馬，仍自被甲，著白布帽，登城西門，招募百姓。

translations.literal: He also sent men to Xinlin to recall the troops of his command, then himself donned armor, put on a white cloth cap, and climbed the western city gate to recruit the common people.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent men to Xinlin to recall his command's troops, then donned armor, put on a white cloth cap, and climbed the western city gate to recruit commoners.

sentences.zh: 是時眾軍並緣江防守，臺內空虛，叔堅乃白太后使太子舍人司馬申以後主命召蕭摩訶，令討之。

translations.literal: At that time the mass of armies were all defending along the river; within the palace it was empty. Shujian then reported to the Empress Dowager, ordering Crown Prince Household Attendant Sima Shen, on Houzhu's command, to summon Xiao Mohe and order him to attack.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the armies were all defending along the river; the palace stood empty. Shujian reported to the empress dowager, ordering crown prince household attendant Sima Shen, on Houzhu's command, to summon Xiao Mohe and order him to attack.

sentences.zh: 即日擒其將戴

translations.literal: That very day he captured Shuling's generals Dai
translations.idiomatic: That very day he captured Shuling's generals Dai

translations.literal: (Xi)
translations.idiomatic: (Xi)

sentences.zh: 〔溫〕、譚騏驎等，〔二七〕送臺，斬于尚書閤下，持其首徇于東城。

translations.literal: Wen, Tan Qilong, and others; they were sent to the capital and beheaded below the Masters of Writing, their heads displayed along the eastern wall.
translations.idiomatic: Wen, Tan Qilong, and others; they were sent to the capital and beheaded below the masters of writing, their heads displayed along the eastern wall.

sentences.zh: 叔陵恇擾不知所為，乃盡殺其妻妾，率左右數百人走趨新林，摩訶追之，斬于丹陽郡，餘黨悉擒。

translations.literal: Shuling, in panic and confusion, did not know what to do; he then killed all his wives and concubines, led several hundred attendants, and fled toward Xinlin. Mohe pursued and beheaded him in Danyang commandery; the remaining partisans were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: Shuling, in panic, did not know what to do; he killed all his wives and concubines, led several hundred attendants, and fled toward Xinlin. Mohe pursued and beheaded him in Danyang commandery; the remaining partisans were all captured.

sentences.zh: 其年，以功進號驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: That year, for his merit he was advanced to Rapid Cavalry General, Grandee Opening the Mansion with Ceremonial Parity to the Three Offices, and Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year, for his merit he was advanced to rapid cavalry general, grandee opening the mansion with ceremonial parity to the three offices, and inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋遷司空，將軍、刺史如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Works, with his general and inspector posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to minister of works, retaining his general and inspector posts.

sentences.zh: 是時後主患創，不能視事，政無小大，悉委叔堅決之，於是勢傾朝廷。

translations.literal: At that time Houzhu was wounded and could not attend to affairs; whether great or small, all government was entrusted to Shujian for decision, and so his power dominated the court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Houzhu was wounded and could not govern; great and small affairs were all entrusted to Shujian, and his power dominated the court.

sentences.zh: 叔堅因肆驕縱，事多不法，後主由是疏而忌之。

translations.literal: Shujian thereupon gave free rein to arrogance and license, and many of his acts were unlawful; Houzhu therefore grew distant and suspicious of him.
translations.idiomatic: Shujian thereupon grew arrogant and lawless; Houzhu therefore grew distant and suspicious of him.

sentences.zh: 孔範、管斌、施文慶之徒，並東宮舊臣，日夜陰持其短。

translations.literal: Kong Fan, Guan Bin, Shi Wenqing, and the like—all old eastern-palace ministers—day and night secretly gathered his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Fan, Guan Bin, Shi Wenqing, and the like—all old eastern-palace ministers—day and night secretly gathered his faults.

sentences.zh: 至德元年，乃詔令即本號用三司之儀，出為江州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide an edict ordered him to use the ceremonial of the Three Offices under his present title and go out as Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 an edict ordered him to use three-office ceremonial under his present title and go out as inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未發，尋有詔又以為驃騎將軍，重為司空，實欲去其權勢。

translations.literal: Before he departed, there was soon another edict making him again Rapid Cavalry General and again Minister of Works—in truth intending to strip away his power.
translations.idiomatic: Before he departed, another edict soon made him again rapid cavalry general and again minister of works—in truth intending to strip away his power.

sentences.zh: 叔堅不自安，稍怨望，乃為左道厭魅以求福助，刻木為偶人，衣以道士之服，施機關，能拜跪，晝夜於日月下醮之，祝詛於上。

translations.literal: Shujian was ill at ease and gradually resentful; he then practiced left-hand ways and malign sorcery to seek blessing, carving wooden puppets, clothing them in Taoist dress, fitting them with mechanisms so they could bow and kneel, offering sacrifices to them day and night under the sun and moon, with curses and imprecations pronounced over them.
translations.idiomatic: Shujian grew uneasy and resentful; he then practiced left-hand sorcery to seek blessing, carving wooden puppets, clothing them in Taoist dress, fitting them with mechanisms so they could bow and kneel, offering sacrifices day and night under sun and moon with curses pronounced over them.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，有人上書告其事，案驗並實，後主召叔堅囚于西省，將殺之。

translations.literal: That winter someone submitted a memorial reporting the affair; investigation proved it all true, and Houzhu summoned Shujian and imprisoned him in the Western Quarters, intending to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: That winter someone memorialized reporting the affair; investigation proved it true, and Houzhu summoned Shujian and imprisoned him in the western quarters, intending to kill him.

sentences.zh: 其夜，令近侍宣敕，數之以罪，叔堅對曰：「臣之本心，非有他故，但欲求親媚耳。

translations.literal: That night he ordered a close attendant to proclaim the edict and enumerate his crimes. Shujian replied, "Your servant's original intent held no other purpose—I only sought to win intimate favor. Your servant has violated Heaven's law and deserves death ten thousand times over; on the day I die I shall surely see Shuling. I beg that the bright edict be proclaimed to reproach him in the realm below the Nine Springs."
translations.idiomatic: That night he ordered a close attendant to proclaim the edict and enumerate his crimes. Shujian replied, "My original intent held no other purpose—I only sought to win intimate favor. I have violated Heaven's law and deserve death ten thousand times over; on the day I die I shall surely see Shuling. I beg that the bright edict be proclaimed to reproach him in the realm below."

sentences.zh: 臣既犯天憲，罪當萬死，臣死之日，必見叔陵，願宣明詔，責於九泉之下。

translations.literal: Houzhu, moved by his former merit, then pardoned him, specially removing him from office and sending him back to his princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu, moved by his former merit, pardoned him, specially removing him from office and sending him back to his residence.

sentences.zh: 」後主感其前功，乃赦之，特免所居官，以王還第。

translations.literal: Soon he was reappointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Suppressing General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was reappointed attendant-in-ordinary and left suppressing general.

sentences.zh: 尋起為侍中、鎮左將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year he was again given drum-and-pipe music and an oil-canopy carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was again given drum-and-pipe music and an oil-canopy carriage.

sentences.zh: 〔二八〕二年，又給鼓吹、油幢車。

translations.literal: In the third year he went out as Campaigning-West General and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he went out as campaigning-west general and inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，出為征西將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was advanced to Central Army Grand General and Grandee Opening the Mansion with Ceremonial Parity to the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was advanced to central army grand general and grandee opening the mansion with ceremonial parity to the three offices.

sentences.zh: 四年，進號中軍大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenming his term expired and he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 2 his term expired and he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 禎明二年，秩滿還都。

translations.literal: In the third year he entered the Pass and was moved to Guazhou; his name was changed to Shuxian.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he entered the Pass and was moved to Guazhou; his name was changed to Shuxian.

sentences.zh: 三年入關，遷于瓜州，更名叔賢。

translations.literal: Shuxian had always been noble and did not know how a household makes its living; by then he and his consort, Lady Shen, sold wine and took in lodgers for hire.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxian had always been noble and did not know how a household makes its living; by then he and his consort, Lady Shen, sold wine and took in lodgers for hire.

sentences.zh: 〔叔〕賢素貴，〔二九〕不知家人生產，至是與妃沈氏酤酒，以傭保為事。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he was made Administrator of Suining commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui's Daye era he was administrator of Suining commandery.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，為遂寧郡太守。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jian'an, Shuqing, styled Zibi, was Emperor Xuan's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shuqing of Jian'an, styled Zibi, was Emperor Xuan's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 建安王叔卿字子弼，高宗第五子也。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and had talent and capacity; his appearance was very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and capable; his appearance was very imposing.

sentences.zh: 性質直有材器，容貌甚偉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taijian he was established as Prince of Jian'an and appointed Eastern Central Commander-in-Chief and Inspector of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 4 he was made Prince of Jian'an and appointed eastern central commander-in-chief and inspector of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 太建四年，立為建安王，授東中郎將、東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was made Cloud-Banner General and Inspector of Yingzhou, with staff clerks appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was made cloud-banner general and inspector of Yingzhou, with staff clerks appointed.

sentences.zh: 七年，為雲麾將軍、郢州刺史，置佐史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was advanced to Pacifying-South General and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he was advanced to pacifying-south general and inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 九年，進號平南將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: When Houzhu succeeded to the throne he was advanced to Pacifying-South General.
translations.idiomatic: When Houzhu succeeded to the throne he was advanced to pacifying-south general.

sentences.zh: 後主即位，進號安南將軍。

translations.literal: He was again made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Suppressing-Right General, and Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made attendant-in-ordinary, suppressing-right general, and director of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又為侍中、鎮右將軍、中書令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supervisor of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷中書監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年入關，隋大業中，為都官郎、上黨通守。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yidu, Shuming, styled Zizhao, was Emperor Xuan's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shuming of Yidu, styled Zizhao, was Emperor Xuan's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 宜都王叔明字子昭，高宗第六子也。

translations.literal: His bearing was beautifully handsome; his manner gentle and weak, in appearance like a woman.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was beautifully handsome; his manner gentle and weak, in appearance like a woman.

sentences.zh: 儀容美麗，舉止和弱，狀似婦人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian he was established as Prince of Yidu and soon appointed Pacifying-Assault General, with staff clerks appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 5 he was made Prince of Yidu and soon appointed pacifying-assault general, with staff clerks appointed.

sentences.zh: 太建五年，立為宜都王，尋授宣惠將軍，置佐史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Eastern Central Commander-in-Chief and Inspector of Dongyang; soon he was made Light-Carriage General and Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was appointed eastern central commander-in-chief and inspector of Dongyang; soon he was made light-carriage general and commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 七年，授東中郎將、東揚州刺史，尋為輕車將軍、衛尉卿。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Cloud-Banner General, and Inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he went out as bearer of the staff, cloud-banner general, and inspector of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十三年，出為使持節、雲麾將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Right Assistant General.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made attendant-in-ordinary and right assistant general.

sentences.zh: 又為侍中、翊右將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhide he was advanced to Pacifying-Right General.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year 4 he was advanced to pacifying-right general.

sentences.zh: 至德四年，進號安右將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the Pass; in the Daye era of Sui he was made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the Pass; under Sui's Daye era he was vice director of the court of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年入關，隋大業中為鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hedong, Shuxian, styled Zigong, was Emperor Xuan's ninth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shuxian of Hedong, styled Zigong, was Emperor Xuan's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 河東王叔獻字子恭，高宗第九子也。

translations.literal: By nature he was respectful and cautious, clever and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was respectful and cautious, clever and fond of learning.

sentences.zh: 性恭謹，聰敏好學。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian he was established as Prince of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 5 he was made Prince of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 太建五年，立為河東王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Pacifying-Assault General, with staff clerks appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was appointed pacifying-assault general, with staff clerks appointed.

sentences.zh: 七年，授宣毅將軍，置佐史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Military Adviser General, and Commander-in-Chief of South Xuzhou Military Affairs and Inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, military adviser general, and commander-in-chief of South Xuzhou military affairs and inspector of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋為散騎常侍、軍師將軍、都督南徐州諸軍事、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died, aged thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he died, aged thirteen.

sentences.zh: 〔三０〕十二年薨，年十三。

translations.literal: [30] In the twelfth year he died, aged thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: [30] In the twelfth year he died, aged thirteen.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、中撫將軍、司空，謚曰康簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted palace attendant, central-secure general, and director of works; posthumous title Kang-jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made palace attendant, central-secure general, and director of works, with the posthumous title Kang-jian.

sentences.zh: 子孝寬嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xiaokuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaokuan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 孝寬以至德元年，襲爵河東王。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan in the first year of Zhide succeeded to the princedom of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 Xiaokuan succeeded as prince of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年入關，隋大業中為汶城令。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the pass; in the Daye era of Sui he was magistrate of Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the pass; under Sui's Daye era he served as magistrate of Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 晉熙王叔文字子才，高宗第十二子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Jinxi Shuwén, styled Zicai, was the twelfth son of Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jinxi Shuwén, styled Zicai, was Emperor Gaozong's twelfth son.

sentences.zh: 性輕險，好虛譽，頗涉書史。

translations.literal: By nature frivolous and rash, he loved empty reputation and was somewhat versed in books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He was frivolous and vain, fond of empty reputation, and had some learning in books and histories.

sentences.zh: 太建七年，立為晉熙王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taijian he was established as Prince of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 7 he was made prince of Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 尋為侍中、散騎常侍、宣惠將軍，置佐史。

translations.literal: Soon he was palace attendant, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and general who spreads grace, with aides and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon palace attendant and regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, with the title general who spreads grace and a full staff.

sentences.zh: 進號輕車將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to general of the light chariot and inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of the light chariot and inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 〔三一〕至德元年，授持節、都督江州諸軍事、江州刺史。

translations.literal: [31] In the first year of Zhide he was given the staff and made area commander over military affairs of Jiangzhou and inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: [31] In Zhide year 1 he received the staff as area commander over Jiangzhou and inspector of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷信威將軍、督湘衡武桂四州諸軍事、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year he was moved to general of trusted might and area commander over the four provinces Xiang, Heng, Wu, and Gui, and inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he became general of trusted might and area commander over Xiang, Heng, Wu, and Gui, with the post of inspector of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 禎明二年，秩滿，徵為侍中、宣毅將軍，佐史如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenming, when his term expired, he was summoned as palace attendant and general of steadfast resolve, his aides and clerks as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 2, when his term ended, he was recalled as palace attendant and general of steadfast resolve, staff unchanged.

sentences.zh: 未還，而隋軍濟江，破臺城，隋漢東道行軍元帥秦王至于漢口。

translations.literal: Before he returned, the Sui army crossed the Yangtze and broke Taicheng; the Sui commander of the eastern Han route, the Prince of Qin, reached Hankou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could return, Sui forces crossed the Yangtze and took Taicheng; the Prince of Qin, commander of the eastern Han route, reached Hankou.

sentences.zh: 時叔文自湘州還朝，至巴州，乃率巴州刺史畢寶等請降，致書於秦王曰：「竊以天無二日，晦明之序不差，土無二王，尊卑之位乃別。

translations.literal: At that time Shuwén was returning from Xiangzhou to court and reached Bazhou; he then led Bazhou inspector Bi Bao and others to request surrender, sending a letter to the Prince of Qin saying: "I venture to observe that Heaven has no second sun, and the sequence of dark and bright does not err; the land has no second king, and the places of high and low are thereby set apart.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwén was then returning from Xiang to court and reached Bazhou; he led Bazhou inspector Bi Bao and others to surrender, writing to the Prince of Qin, "Heaven has but one sun and the order of night and day never fails; the realm has but one king and rank is thereby fixed.

sentences.zh: 今車書混壹，文軌大同，敢披丹款，申其屈膝。

translations.literal: Now carriage and writing are unified and culture and tracks are one; I dare lay open my red sincerity and declare my bent knee."
translations.idiomatic: Now empire and script are one and the ways of court and countryside are joined; I dare lay bare my loyalty and bow the knee."

sentences.zh: 」秦王得書，因遣行軍吏部柳莊與元帥府僚屬等往巴州迎勞叔文。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin received the letter and sent Xingjun's director of the ministry of personnel Liu Zhuang, with staff of the prince's headquarters and others, to Bazhou to welcome and comfort Shuwén.
translations.idiomatic: The prince received the letter and sent Liu Zhuang of the ministry of personnel, with headquarters staff, to Bazhou to welcome Shuwén.

sentences.zh: 叔文於是與畢寶、荊州刺史陳紀及文武將吏赴于漢口，秦王並厚待之，置于賓館。
