translations.literal: Shuwén thereupon, with Bi Bao, Jingzhou inspector Chen Ji, and civil and military officers, went to Hankou; the Prince of Qin all treated them generously and lodged them in the guest house.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwén then went to Hankou with Bi Bao, Jingzhou inspector Chen Ji, and his civil and military officers; the prince received them generously and lodged them in the guest quarters.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇九年三月，眾軍凱旋，文帝親幸溫湯勞之，叔文與陳紀、周羅睺、荀法尚等并諸降人，見于路次。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year of Sui's Kaihuang era the armies returned in triumph; Emperor Wen personally went to the hot springs to reward them; Shuwén, with Chen Ji, Zhou Luohou, Xun Fashang, and the other submitters, were seen along the route.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kaihuang year 9 the armies returned in triumph; Emperor Wen went in person to the hot springs to reward them, and Shuwén, Chen Ji, Zhou Luohou, Xun Fashang, and the other submitters were presented along the road.

sentences.zh: 數日，叔文從後主及諸王侯將相并乘輿、服御、天文圖籍等，並以次行列，仍以鐵騎圍之，隨晉王、秦王等獻凱而入，列于廟庭。

translations.literal: Several days later Shuwén followed Houzhu and the kings, marquises, generals, and ministers, with chariots, robes, astronomical charts and records, and the rest, each in order and rank; iron cavalry surrounded them as they followed the Prince of Jin, the Prince of Qin, and the others in presenting triumph and entering, arrayed in the court of the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Shuwén followed Houzhu and the princes, marquises, generals, and ministers, with chariots, regalia, charts, and records, each in rank; iron cavalry ringed them as they marched with the princes of Jin and Qin in triumphal entry and were ranged in the temple court.

sentences.zh: 明日，隋文帝坐于廣陽門觀，叔文又從後主至朝堂南，文帝使內史令李德林宣旨，責其君臣不能相弼，以致喪亡。

translations.literal: The next day Emperor Wen of Sui sat at Guangyang Gate to observe; Shuwén again followed Houzhu to the south of the audience hall; Emperor Wen had Secretariat Director Li Delin proclaim the decree, rebuking their ruler and ministers for failing to support one another and thereby bringing ruin.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Emperor Wen sat at Guangyang Gate to review them; Shuwén again followed Houzhu to the south of the audience hall while Li Delin, director of the secretariat, proclaimed a decree rebuking ruler and ministers for failing one another and bringing the state to ruin.

sentences.zh: 後主與其群臣並慚懼拜伏，莫能仰視，叔文獨欣然而有自得之志。

translations.literal: Houzhu and his ministers all bowed in shame and fear, none daring to look up; Shuwén alone was pleased and had the air of self-satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu and his ministers bowed in shame and fear, none daring to raise their eyes; Shuwén alone looked pleased, as if satisfied with himself.

sentences.zh: 旬有六日，乃上表曰：「昔在巴州，已先送款，乞知此情，望異常例。

translations.literal: Sixteen days later he submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly at Bazhou I had already sent my submission first; I beg to know this circumstance and hope for an exceptional case."
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen days later he memorialized, "At Bazhou I had already submitted first; I beg that this be known and that I receive exceptional treatment."

sentences.zh: 」文帝雖嫌其不忠，而方欲懷柔江表，乃授開府，拜宜州刺史。

translations.literal: Though Emperor Wen resented his disloyalty, he was then wishing to soothe the lands south of the Yangtze and therefore granted an establishment and made him inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor resented his disloyalty, he still wished to soothe the south and therefore granted him an establishment and made him inspector of Yi.

sentences.zh: 淮南王叔彪字子華，高宗第十三子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Huainan Shubiao, styled Zihua, was the thirteenth son of Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Huainan Shubiao, styled Zihua, was Emperor Gaozong's thirteenth son.

sentences.zh: 少聰惠，善屬文。

translations.literal: In youth intelligent and clever, skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was clever and skilled at writing.

sentences.zh: 太建八年，立為淮南王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taijian he was established as Prince of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 8 he was made prince of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 尋位侍中、仁威將軍，置佐史。

translations.literal: Soon he was palace attendant and general of humane might, with aides and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon palace attendant and general of humane might, with a staff.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年入關，卒于長安。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the pass and died at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the pass and died at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 始興王叔重字子厚，高宗第十四子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Shixing Shuzhong, styled Zihou, was the fourteenth son of Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shixing Shuzhong, styled Zihou, was Emperor Gaozong's fourteenth son.

sentences.zh: 性質朴，無伎藝。

translations.literal: By nature simple and plain, without arts or skills.
translations.idiomatic: He was plain by nature and without special talents.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，始興王叔陵為逆，誅死，其年立叔重為始興王，以奉昭烈王後。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong died, Prince of Shixing Shuling rebelled and was executed; that year Shuzhong was established as Prince of Shixing to continue the line of Prince Zhao-lie.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong died, Prince of Shixing Shuling rebelled and was put to death; that year Shuzhong was made prince of Shixing to continue Prince Zhao-lie's line.

sentences.zh: 至德元年，為仁威將軍、揚州刺史，置佐史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was general of humane might and inspector of Yangzhou, with aides and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 he was general of humane might and inspector of Yangzhou, with a staff.

sentences.zh: 二年，加使持節、都督江州諸軍事、江州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year he was given the added staff and made area commander over military affairs of Jiangzhou and inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he received the staff as area commander over Jiangzhou and inspector of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年入關。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the pass.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the pass.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中為太府少卿，卒。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he was vice director of the grand treasury and died.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui's Daye era he was vice director of the grand treasury and died.

sentences.zh: 尋陽王叔儼字子思，高宗第十五子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Xunyang Shuyan, styled Zisi, was the fifteenth son of Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xunyang Shuyan, styled Zisi, was Emperor Gaozong's fifteenth son.

sentences.zh: 性凝重，舉止方正。

translations.literal: By nature grave and weighty, his bearing and conduct were square and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Grave in nature, his bearing was square and upright.

sentences.zh: 後主即位，立為尋陽王。

translations.literal: When Houzhu succeeded to the throne he was established as Prince of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Houzhu took the throne he was made prince of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 至德元年，為侍中、仁武將軍，置佐史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was palace attendant and general of humane martiality, with aides and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 he was palace attendant and general of humane martiality, with a staff.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年入關，尋卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered the pass and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the pass and soon died.

sentences.zh: 三年，隋師濟江，破臺城，前刺史晉熙王叔文還至巴州，與巴州刺史畢寶、荊州刺史陳紀並降。

translations.literal: In year three, when the Sui army crossed the Yangtze and broke Taicheng, the former inspector Prince of Jinxi Shuwén returned to Bazhou and, with Bazhou inspector Bi Bao and Jingzhou inspector Chen Ji, all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, when Sui forces crossed the Yangtze and took Taicheng, the former inspector Prince of Jinxi Shuwén returned to Bazhou and surrendered with Bazhou inspector Bi Bao and Jingzhou inspector Chen Ji.

sentences.zh: 隋行軍元帥清河公楊素兵下荊門，別遣其將龐暉將兵略地，南至湘州，城內將士，莫有固志，克日請降。

translations.literal: The Sui campaign commander Duke of Qinghe Yang Su led troops down Jingmen and separately sent his general Pang Hui with troops to overrun the land, south to Xiangzhou; within the city none had a mind to hold firm, and on the appointed day they requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Sui commander Duke of Qinghe Yang Su marched down Jingmen and sent his general Pang Hui south to Xiangzhou; none in the city would stand firm, and they asked to surrender on the set day.

sentences.zh: 叔慎乃置酒會文武僚吏，酒酣，叔慎歎曰「君臣之義，盡於此乎！

translations.literal: Shushen thereupon set wine and feasted the civil and military officers; when the wine was deep, Shushen sighed and said, "The righteousness of ruler and minister ends here, does it not!"
translations.idiomatic: Shushen then set wine for his civil and military officers; when they were deep in drink he sighed, "The bond of ruler and minister ends here, does it not!"

sentences.zh: 」長史謝基伏而流涕，湘州助防遂興侯正理在坐，乃起曰：「主辱臣死，諸君獨非陳國之臣乎？

translations.literal: Chief steward Xie Ji lay prostrate weeping; the Xiangzhou assistant for defense, Marquis of Suixing Zheng Lili, who was present, then rose and said, "When the lord is shamed the minister dies—are you alone not Chen ministers?
translations.idiomatic: Chief steward Xie Ji lay prostrate weeping; Xiangzhou's assistant for defense, Marquis of Suixing Zheng Lili, who was present, rose and said, "When the lord is shamed the minister must die—are you not all Chen ministers?

sentences.zh: 今天下有難，實是致命之秋也。

translations.literal: Now the realm has difficulty; this is truly the season to give one's life.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is in peril; this is truly the hour to give one's life.

sentences.zh: 縱其無成，猶見臣節，青門之外，有死不能。

translations.literal: Even if there is no success, one still shows the minister's integrity; beyond the Green Gate there is death one cannot refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Even without success we may yet show a minister's integrity; beyond the Green Gate there is death one cannot refuse.

sentences.zh: 今日之機，不可猶豫，後應者斬。

translations.literal: Today's opportunity cannot be hesitated over; whoever follows afterward shall be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Today's chance cannot be hesitated over; whoever holds back shall be beheaded."

sentences.zh: 」眾咸許諾，乃刑牲結盟。

translations.literal: The crowd all promised; they then slaughtered a victim and formed an alliance.
translations.idiomatic: All assented; they slaughtered a victim and swore an oath.

sentences.zh: 仍遣人詐奉降書於龐暉，暉信之，克期而入，叔慎伏甲待之。

translations.literal: They then sent a man to feign a surrender letter to Pang Hui; Hui believed it and, on the agreed day, entered; Shushen had armed men wait in ambush.
translations.idiomatic: They sent a man with a false surrender letter to Pang Hui; Hui believed it and entered on the agreed day while Shushen's men lay in ambush.

sentences.zh: 暉令數百人屯于城門，自將左右數十人入于廳事，俄而伏兵發，縛暉以徇，盡擒其黨，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Hui ordered several hundred men to camp at the city gate; he himself led several tens of men into the hall; soon the ambush sprang, they bound Hui and paraded him, seized all his party, and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Hui left several hundred men at the gate and led a few dozen into the hall; the ambush sprang, they bound Hui and paraded him through the streets, seized his party, and beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 叔慎坐于射堂，招合士眾，數日之中，兵至五千人。

translations.literal: Shushen sat in the archery hall and gathered soldiers; within several days troops reached five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Shushen sat in the archery hall and gathered troops; within days his force reached five thousand.

sentences.zh: 衡陽太守樊通、武州刺史鄔居業，皆請赴難。

translations.literal: Hengyang prefect Fan Tong and Wuzhou inspector Wu Juye both requested to come to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Hengyang prefect Fan Tong and Wuzhou inspector Wu Juye both asked to march to his aid.

sentences.zh: 未至，隋遣中牟公薛冑為湘州刺史，聞龐暉死，乃益請兵，隋又遣行軍總管劉仁恩救之。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Sui sent Duke of Zhongmou Xue Zhou as inspector of Xiangzhou; hearing of Pang Hui's death, he asked for more troops, and Sui also sent campaign commander Liu Ren'en to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived, Sui appointed Duke of Zhongmou Xue Zhou inspector of Xiang; hearing Pang Hui was dead, he asked for reinforcements, and Sui also sent campaign commander Liu Ren'en.

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Xue Zhou's troops halted at Goose-Sheep Mountain; Shushen sent Zheng Lili and Fan Tong and others to resist them; a great battle was joined from dawn until the sun slanted, the Sui army resting and fighting in turns, while Zheng Lili's troops were few and could not match—thereupon they were greatly defeated.

sentences.zh: 是時，鄔居業率其眾自武州來赴，出橫橋江，聞叔慎敗績，乃頓于新康口。

translations.literal: At the time Houzhu was already grown and had no heir by Yin; Emperor Gaozong therefore ordered that he be made legitimate grandson, and that same day an edict said: "The imperial grandson is newly born and the state's fortune is just rising; We wish to share this joy with the ministers. sentences.zh: 胤性聰敏，好學，執經肄業，終日不倦，博通大義，兼善屬文。

translations.literal: Yin by nature was clever and loved learning; he held the classics and pursued his studies, never weary all day, broadly penetrating great principles and also skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was clever and loved learning; he held the classics and studied all day without weariness, broadly penetrating great principles and also skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 至德三年，躬出太學講孝經，講畢，又釋奠於先聖先師。

translations.literal: At this time Consort Zhang and Honored Concubine Kong were both favored; Empress Shen had no favor, yet attendants close at hand repeatedly went to and from the Eastern Palace, and the heir apparent also repeatedly sent men to the empress's quarters. Houzhu suspected resentment and ill will and greatly hated this.

translations.idiomatic: On "[8] in year seven transferred to General Who Wins the Championship and Central Leader of the Gentlemen": Emperor Xuan's annals place Boren as central leader in the eleventh month of Taijian year 8.

sentences.zh: 〔九〕 禎明元年加侍中 「侍中」後主紀作「特進」。

translations.literal: [9] In Zhenming year 1 made Attendant-in-Ordinary—"attendant-in-ordinary" in Houzhu's annals reads "special advancement."
translations.idiomatic: On "[9] in Zhenming year 1 made Attendant-in-Ordinary": Houzhu's annals read special advancement for attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 〔一０〕太建初至合州刺史 按宣帝紀，伯義於太建九年七月以輕車將軍、丹陽尹為合州刺史，十年九月以宣惠將軍為東揚州刺史，均不在太建初，官職遷轉，亦不盡合。

translations.literal: [10] From early Taijian to Inspector of Hezhou—according to the Annals of Emperor Xuan, Boyi in the seventh month of Taijian year 9 as General of Light Chariots and Administrator of Danyang became Inspector of Hezhou; in the ninth month of year 10 as General Who Propagates Favor became Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou—neither was in early Taijian, and the career shifts do not all match.
translations.idiomatic: On "[10] from early Taijian to Inspector of Hezhou": Emperor Xuan's annals have Boyi made Hezhou inspector in the seventh month of Taijian year 9 and Eastern Yangzhou inspector in the ninth month of year 10—not early Taijian—and the posts do not all align.

sentences.zh: 〔一一〕御史中丞徐君敷奏曰 「徐君敷」南史作「徐君整」。

translations.literal: [11] Censor-in-Chief Xu Junfu memorialized—"Xu Junfu" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Xu Junzheng."
translations.idiomatic: On "[11] Censor-in-Chief Xu Junfu memorialized": the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Xu Junzheng.

sentences.zh: 〔一二〕早擅英猷 「早」南監本作「夙」，北監本、汲本、殿本作「昔」。

translations.literal: [12] Early famed for heroic plans—in the Southern Supervisory edition "early" reads "from of old"; the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions read "formerly."
translations.idiomatic: On "[12] early famed for heroic plans": the Southern Supervisory edition reads from of old; the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions read formerly.

sentences.zh: 〔一三〕太建中立為永陽王 按帝紀，立伯智為永陽王在廢帝光大二年，不在太建中。

translations.literal: [13] Established as Prince of Yongyang in Taijian—according to the imperial annals, establishing Bozhi as Prince of Yongyang was in the second year of Guangda under the deposed emperor, not in Taijian.
translations.idiomatic: On "[13] established as Prince of Yongyang in Taijian": the annals place establishing Bozhi as Prince of Yongyang in deposed-emperor Guangda year 2, not Taijian.

sentences.zh: 〔一四〕累遷尚書左僕射 按後主紀，伯智於後主即位之年三月為尚書僕射，至德二年五月，又以尚書僕射為平東將軍、東揚州刺史，兩言僕射，均無「左」字。

translations.literal: [14] Advanced step by step to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing—according to Houzhu's annals, Bozhi in the third month of the year Houzhu succeeded became Director of the Masters of Writing; in the fifth month of Zhide year 2 he was again made Director of the Masters of Writing while serving as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou—both mentions of director lack the character "left."
translations.idiomatic: On "[14] advanced to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing": Houzhu's annals make Bozhi director of the masters of writing in the third month of his accession year and again in Zhide year 2, fifth month—neither has left.

sentences.zh: 〔一五〕都督東揚豐二州諸軍事 「豐」原訛「曹」，各本不訛，今改正。

translations.literal: [15] Commissioner over Eastern Yang and Feng—"Feng" was originally corrupt as "Cao"; no edition errs; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On "[15] commissioner over Eastern Yang and Feng": Feng was originally written Cao; no edition errs; now corrected.

sentences.zh: 按廢帝光大二年四月，割東揚州晉安郡為豐州。

translations.literal: According to the second year of Guangda under the deposed emperor, fourth month, Jin'an commandery of Eastern Yangzhou was split off as Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In deposed-emperor Guangda year 2, fourth month, Jin'an commandery of Eastern Yangzhou was split off as Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 〔一六〕太建中立為桂陽王 按帝紀，立伯茂為桂陽王在廢帝光大二年七月，不在太建中。

translations.literal: [16] Established as Prince of Guiyang in Taijian—according to the imperial annals, establishing Bomao as Prince of Guiyang was in the seventh month of Guangda year 2 under the deposed emperor, not in Taijian.
translations.idiomatic: On "[16] established as Prince of Guiyang in Taijian": the annals place establishing Bomao as Prince of Guiyang in deposed-emperor Guangda year 2, seventh month—not Taijian.

sentences.zh: 〔一七〕魏昭容生建安王叔卿 「魏昭容」南史作「魏昭華」。

translations.literal: [17] Lady of Bright Talent Wei bore Prince of Jian'an Shuqing—"Lady of Bright Talent Wei" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Lady of Bright Talent Wei [Hua]."
translations.idiomatic: On "[17] Lady of Bright Talent Wei bore Prince of Jian'an Shuqing": the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Lady of Bright Talent Wei Hua.

sentences.zh: 〔一八〕巴山王叔雄 「叔雄」後主紀作「叔熊」，參閱第六卷校記第五條。

translations.literal: [18] Prince of Bashan Shuxiong—"Shuxiong" in Houzhu's annals reads "Shuxiong [Bear]"; see Collation Note 5 in Volume 6.
translations.idiomatic: On "[18] Prince of Bashan Shuxiong": Houzhu's annals read Shuxiong (Bear); see Collation Note 5 in Volume 6.

sentences.zh: 〔一九〕劉姬生臨江王叔顯 「臨江王」北監本、汲本、殿本作「臨海王」，南史同。

translations.literal: [19] Lady Liu bore Prince of Linjiang Shuxian—"Prince of Linjiang" in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads "Prince of Linhai"; the History of the Southern Dynasties agrees.
translations.idiomatic: On "[19] Lady Liu bore Prince of Linjiang Shuxian": the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties read Prince of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 按後主紀，至德四年二月丙申，立皇弟叔顯為臨江王，各本及南史並同，無作「臨海王」者，當以作「臨江王」為是。

translations.literal: According to Houzhu's annals, on bingchen of the second month of Zhide year 4, the emperor's younger brother Shuxian was established as Prince of Linjiang; all editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties agree; none read Prince of Linhai; Prince of Linjiang should stand.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu's annals record Shuxian established as Prince of Linjiang on bingchen, second month, Zhide year 4; all editions and the Southern History agree—Linjiang, not Linhai, is correct.

sentences.zh: 〔二０〕叔

translations.literal: [20] Prince
translations.idiomatic: [20] Prince

translations.literal: (yin)
translations.idiomatic: (yin)

sentences.zh: 〔弘〕 據北監本、汲本、殿本改。

translations.literal: [Hong]—changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "[Hong]": emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.

sentences.zh: 按宋刻本因避諱，「弘」字皆缺筆，往往訛作「引」。

translations.literal: Comment: in the Song engraved edition, to avoid taboo the character "Hong" is always written with a missing stroke and often corrupts as "yin."
translations.idiomatic: The Song engraved edition, avoiding taboo, writes Hong with a missing stroke, often corrupting to yin.

sentences.zh: 然此「弘」字疑當依南史作「泓」，因豫章王叔英之長子名弘，不當犯其叔父之名諱也。

translations.literal: Yet this "Hong" probably should follow the History of the Southern Dynasties as "Hong [Vast]," because Prince of Yuzhang Shuying's eldest son was named Hong and should not violate his uncle's name taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this Hong probably should follow the Southern History as Hong (vast), since Prince of Yuzhang Shuying's eldest son was named Hong and must not violate his uncle's taboo.

sentences.zh: 〔二一〕五年進號平北將軍南豫州刺史 「南豫州」宣帝紀作「南徐州」。

translations.literal: [21] In year 5 advanced to General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou—"Southern Yuzhou" in the Annals of Emperor Xuan reads "Southern Xuzhou."
translations.idiomatic: On "[21] in year 5 advanced to General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou": Emperor Xuan's annals read Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 似當從紀文。

translations.literal: Probably one should follow the annals.
translations.idiomatic: The annals text is probably correct.

sentences.zh: 〔二二〕十一年為鎮前將軍江州刺史 「鎮前將軍」當依宣帝紀作「 鎮南將軍」。

translations.literal: [22] In year 11 made General Who Guards the Front and Inspector of Jiangzhou—"General Who Guards the Front" should follow the Annals of Emperor Xuan as "General Who Guards the South."
translations.idiomatic: On "[22] in year 11 made General Who Guards the Front and Inspector of Jiangzhou": Emperor Xuan's annals read General Who Guards the South.

sentences.zh: 按「鎮前」之號用於內，不應冠江州刺史之上。

translations.literal: Comment: the title General Who Guards the Front is used internally and should not crown the post of Jiangzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Guards the Front is an inner-court rank and should not head the Jiangzhou inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 〔二三〕四年進號驃騎大將軍 按此「大」字疑衍。

translations.literal: [23] In year 4 advanced to Cavalry General-in-Chief—this character "grand" is suspected as a spurious addition.
translations.idiomatic: On "[23] in year 4 advanced to Cavalry General-in-Chief": the character grand is probably spurious.

sentences.zh: 詳第六卷校記第十四條。

translations.literal: See Collation Note 14 in Volume 6.
translations.idiomatic: See Collation Note 14 in Volume 6.

sentences.zh: 〔二四〕其年遷司空 「司空」後主紀作「司徒」。

translations.literal: [24] That year transferred to Minister of Works—"Minister of Works" in Houzhu's annals reads "Minister over the Masses."
translations.idiomatic: On "[24] that year transferred to Minister of Works": Houzhu's annals read Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 〔二五〕尋為平北將軍合州刺史 按宣帝紀，叔堅為合州刺史，進號平北將軍，在太建八年六月。

translations.literal: [25] Soon made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hezhou—according to the Annals of Emperor Xuan, Shujian as Inspector of Hezhou with advancement to General Who Pacifies the North was in the sixth month of Taijian year 8.
translations.idiomatic: On "[25] soon made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hezhou": Emperor Xuan's annals place Shujian's Hezhou inspectorship and advancement in the sixth month of Taijian year 8.

sentences.zh: 〔二六〕入為翊左將軍丹陽尹 按後主紀，後主即位，以侍中、翊前將軍、丹陽尹長沙王叔堅為驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: [26] Entered court as General of the Left Guard and Administrator of Danyang—according to Houzhu's annals, when Houzhu succeeded, Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Front Guard and Administrator of Danyang Prince of Changsha Shujian was made Cavalry General-in-Chief, Opening the Government, Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, and Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On "[26] entered court as General of the Left Guard and Administrator of Danyang": Houzhu's annals make Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Front Guard, and Danyang administrator Prince of Changsha Shujian cavalry general-in-chief with equal honor and Yangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 「 翊左」作「翊前」。

translations.literal: "General of the Left Guard" should read "General of the Front Guard."
translations.idiomatic: General of the Left Guard should read General of the Front Guard.

sentences.zh: 〔二七〕即日擒其將戴

translations.literal: [27] That day captured his generals Dai
translations.idiomatic: [27] That day captured his generals Dai

translations.literal: (xi)
translations.idiomatic: (xi)

sentences.zh: 〔溫〕譚騏驎等 據南監本改。

translations.literal: [Wen] and Tan Qilin and the rest—changed according to the Southern Supervisory edition.
translations.idiomatic: On "[Wen] and Tan Qilin and the rest": emended per the Southern Supervisory edition.

sentences.zh: 按通鑑陳宣帝太建十四年亦作「戴溫」。

translations.literal: Comment: the Comprehensive Mirror for Emperor Xuan of Chen, Taijian year 14, also reads "Dai Wen."
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Emperor Xuan Taijian year 14, also reads Dai Wen.

sentences.zh: 〔二八〕尋起為侍中鎮左將軍 按後主紀，叔堅為侍中、鎮左將軍在至德二年七月。

translations.literal: [28] Soon restored as Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Left Guard—according to Houzhu's annals, Shujian as Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Left Guard was in the seventh month of Zhide year 2.
translations.idiomatic: On "[28] soon restored as Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Left Guard": Houzhu's annals place this in the seventh month of Zhide year 2.

sentences.zh: 〔二九〕〔叔〕賢素貴 據北監本、汲本、殿本補。

translations.literal: [29] [Shu]xian had always been noble—supplemented according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "[29] [Shu]xian had always been noble": restored per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.

sentences.zh: 按叔堅更名叔賢，避隋文帝楊堅諱。

translations.literal: Comment: Shujian changed his name to Shuxian to avoid the taboo on Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Shujian renamed himself Shuxian to avoid taboo on Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian.

sentences.zh: 〔三０〕尋為散騎常侍至南徐州刺史 按宣帝紀，叔獻為南徐州刺史在太建十二年四月。

translations.literal: [30] Soon made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary through Inspector of Southern Xuzhou—according to the Annals of Emperor Xuan, Shuxian as Inspector of Southern Xuzhou was in the fourth month of Taijian year 12.
translations.idiomatic: On "[30] soon made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary through Inspector of Southern Xuzhou": Emperor Xuan's annals place Shuxian as Southern Xuzhou inspector in the fourth month of Taijian year 12.

sentences.zh: 〔三一〕進號輕車將軍揚州刺史 按後主紀，叔文為揚州刺史在至德元年正月。

translations.literal: [31] Advanced to General of Light Chariots and Inspector of Yangzhou—according to Houzhu's annals, Shuwen as Inspector of Yangzhou was in the first month of Zhide year 1.
translations.idiomatic: On "[31] advanced to General of Light Chariots and Inspector of Yangzhou": Houzhu's annals place Shuwen as Yangzhou inspector in the first month of Zhide year 1.

sentences.zh: 〔三二〕新興王叔純字子共 「子共」南史作「子洪」。

translations.literal: [32] Prince of Xinxing Shuchun, styled Zigong—"Zigong" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Zihong."
translations.idiomatic: On "[32] Prince of Xinxing Shuchun, styled Zigong": the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Zihong.

sentences.zh: 〔三三〕巴東王叔謨字子軌 張森楷校勘記云：「『謨』疑當作『模』，與其字子軌相稱。」

translations.literal: [33] Prince of Badong Shumo, styled Zigui—Zhang Senkai's collation note says: "'Shumo' is probably 'Shumo [Model],' matching the style name Zigui."
translations.idiomatic: On "[33] Prince of Badong Shumo, styled Zigui": Zhang Senkai's note says Shumo is probably Shumo (model), matching Zigui.

sentences.zh: 〔三四〕臨江王叔顯字子明 「子明」南史作「子亮」。

translations.literal: [34] Prince of Linjiang Shuxian, styled Ziming—"Ziming" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Ziliang."
translations.idiomatic: On "[34] Prince of Linjiang Shuxian, styled Ziming": the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 〔三五〕進號安南將軍 「安南將軍」後主紀禎明二年作「安北將軍」。

translations.literal: [35] Advanced to General Who Pacifies the South—"General Who Pacifies the South" in Houzhu's annals for Zhenming year 2 reads "General Who Pacifies the North."
translations.idiomatic: On "[35] advanced to General Who Pacifies the South": Houzhu's annals for Zhenming year 2 read General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 〔三六〕平南將軍江州刺史 「平南將軍」後主紀禎明二年作「安南將軍」。

translations.literal: [36] General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jiangzhou—"General Who Pacifies the South" in Houzhu's annals for Zhenming year 2 reads "General of Pacified South."
translations.idiomatic: On "[36] General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jiangzhou": Houzhu's annals for Zhenming year 2 read General of Pacified South.

sentences.zh: 〔三七〕出為平北將軍南徐州刺史 「平北將軍」後主紀作「安北將軍」。

translations.literal: [37] Sent out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou—"General Who Pacifies the North" in Houzhu's annals reads "General of Pacified North."
translations.idiomatic: On "[37] sent out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou": Houzhu's annals read General of Pacified North.

sentences.zh: 〔三八〕隋大業中為

translations.literal: [38] Under the Sui's Daye era he was
translations.idiomatic: [38] Under the Sui's Daye era he was

translations.literal: (hui)
translations.idiomatic: (hui)

sentences.zh: 昌〔隆〕令 據南史改。

translations.literal: [Long] magistrate of Chang—changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: On "[Long] magistrate of Chang": emended per the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 按隋志無會昌縣。

translations.literal: Comment: the Sui Treatises have no Huichang county.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui Treatises list no Huichang county.
